text:
Maria P: Incoming escalation from ACME: their app saw repeated cross-region failovers over the last 20m, users hitting eu-west but getting routed to us-east, massive latency spikes. customer ticket #7421.
Alex K: ugh, do we have correlation ids or request ids from their traces?
Maria P: yes, shared one: req_id=8a3f2c. They saw a routing flip at 1719499827, then again at 1719499940.
Jin L: any recent routing or healthcheck changes? I rolled heartbeat tuning in PR #4896 yesterday to reduce alert noise.
Alex K: that PR changed probe grace from 10s -> 5s right? Could cause short GC/rumps to appear as failures.
Maria P: customer reports the edge probe returned 503 for ~3s before failover. probe path is /health/live. runtime readiness is on /ready.
Oncall SRE: if probes hit /health/live but runtime returns 200, then ok. We need exact probe responses. Maria, can you paste the edge probe logs?
Maria P: here's the relevant tail from the edge agent (sanitized):
```
[2024-06-15T12:17:07Z] probe /health/live -> 503 (conn reset)
[2024-06-15T12:17:09Z] probe /health/live -> 200
[2024-06-15T12:17:10Z] failover triggered to fallback-region
```
Jin L: hmm 2s 503 then 200 then failover at +3s. That smells like our heartbeat debounce/TTL not aligned with edge probe frequency. What is probe interval?
Alex K: edge probes run every 1s, debounce window was 3 failures -> 3s, and we lowered grace to 2? Let me check config:
```
edge.probe.interval=1000
edge.probe.debounce_failures=3
edge.failover.grace=2000
```
Maria P: customer says their service had brief CPU spike (~70% CPU) on host, GC pause maybe. So 2–3s glitch is plausible. But failover should not flip on transients.
Oncall SRE: we should disable automatic cross-region failover for this customer's route while we investigate. Can we set route-level failover_policy=hold?
Alex K: done for customer ACME-route-17, set to manual at 1719500060.
deploy-bot: rollback of heartbeat-tuning PR #4896 scheduled to canary lane at commit 1f4b2c (deployer: Jin).
Jin L: repro steps I used locally: 1) start a server returning 200; 2) simulate a short 2s stall where probe returns 503; 3) observe edge metrics. I can share a quick script.
Maria P: pls share script and I'll try to repro against their environment (with their consent). Also sending customer a temp mitigation summary.
Alex K: quick command to emulate probe failure against our edge:
```
# simulate bad probe
curl -X GET "https://edge-host/route/ACME-route-17/health/live" -H "X-Test-Fail: 1"
```
Jin L: script attached in thread (snippet):
```
# fragile emulation
for i in $(seq 1 5); do
  if [ $i -eq 3 ]; then
    # return 503 for a short window
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "X-Test-Fail: 1" https://edge-host/health/live
  else
    curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://edge-host/health/live
  fi
  sleep 1
done
```
Oncall SRE: next steps: 1) keep failover manual for ACME; 2) roll back heartbeat-tuning from canary if canary shows flap; 3) add an extended debounce for cross-region failover (5s) and keep edge probe interval same; 4) follow up with ACME with timeline and temporary mitigation.
Maria P: creating a postmortem draft and will include timestamps + trace ids. Adding action item to add a synthetic Canary that simulates transient 2s failures.
Alex K: also add metric: consecutive_failed_probes_before_failover per-route so we can alert if it's too low.
Jin L: I'll watch canary rollout and report within 30m.
Maria P: thanks team. Updating ticket #7421 and pinging customer that we put failover to manual and are investigating. :thumbsup:
